theorems.name: Durrleman's Condition for Raw SVI as a Finite Polynomial-Sign Formula
theorems.description: For the five-parameter raw SVI total variance, a fixed finite Boolean combination of signs of polynomials in (a, b, rho, m, sigma) holds exactly when sigma > 0, b >= 0, rho^2 <= 1, the variance is positive at every log-strike, and Durrleman's function g is nonnegative at every log-strike. Repeated roots, constant and degenerate numerator polynomials, b = 0 and rho = +-1 are covered. The formula is defined structurally, as the expansion of a finite sign program, and is not written out as a list of inequalities; the zero-scale case sigma = 0 is in mf-svi-strike-convexity-sign-formula.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.ExtendedFormula

open MathFin MathFin.SVI Set

/-- **Durrleman's condition for raw SVI as a finite sign formula.** `fullCertificateFormula`, a
    fixed finite Boolean combination of signs of polynomials in the five parameters, holds at `p`
    exactly when `σ > 0`, `b ≥ 0`, `ρ² ≤ 1`, the total variance is positive at every log-strike,
    and Durrleman's function is nonnegative at every log-strike. Re-export of
    `MathFin.SVI.fullCertificateFormula_iff`. -/
theorem svi_durrleman_sign_formula (p : Params) :
    fullCertificateFormula.eval p = true ↔
      0 < p.sigma ∧ 0 ≤ p.b ∧ 0 ≤ 1 - p.rho ^ 2 ∧
        (∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) ∧ (∀ k : ℝ, 0 ≤ durrleman p k) :=
  fullCertificateFormula_iff p

metadata.formalization_scope: Re-export of MathFin.SVI.fullCertificateFormula_iff. The raw SVI total variance is w(k) = a + b(rho(k-m) + sqrt((k-m)^2 + sigma^2)) and Durrleman's function g is built from its actual first and second derivatives (Derivatives.lean). The formula is a SignFormula over MvPolynomial (Fin 5) R, defined structurally as the expansion of a finite sign program (degree branch, four Hermite-matrix signatures by characteristic sign variations); it is not printed as an expanded list of inequalities. Proof route: rationalise g to a degree-ten polynomial on (0, infinity); nonnegativity there iff endpoint signs and no negative critical value; count those by four Tarski queries; evaluate each by Hermite's trace-form signature identity, proved for arbitrary nonzero f without squarefreeness; clear denominators. SCOPE. Smooth case sigma > 0 only. Strictly positive variance at every finite log-strike is part of the characterised domain; slices with zero variance somewhere are excluded. No statement about calendar-spread arbitrage or about surfaces.

theorems.name: Durrleman's Condition is Convexity of the SVI-Smiled Call in Strike
theorems.description: For raw SVI with sigma > 0 and total variance positive at every log-strike, the Black–Scholes call price with the SVI volatility substituted strike by strike (spot, maturity and discount factor normalised to one) is convex in strike on (0, infinity) if and only if Durrleman's function g is nonnegative at every log-strike. The price is MathFin's bsV evaluated at the smile, not a constant-volatility derivative.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.ExtendedFormula

open MathFin MathFin.SVI Set

/-- **Durrleman's condition is convexity of the call in strike.** For raw SVI with `σ > 0` and
    positive total variance, the Black–Scholes call with the SVI volatility substituted strike by
    strike (spot, maturity and discount factor one) is convex on `(0, ∞)` exactly when Durrleman's
    function is nonnegative at every log-strike. Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.bsSmile_convex_iff`. -/
theorem svi_call_convex_iff_durrleman (p : Params) (hs : 0 < p.sigma)
    (hw : ∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) :
    ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) (bsSmile p) ↔ ∀ k : ℝ, 0 ≤ durrleman p k :=
  bsSmile_convex_iff p hs hw

theorems.name: The Durrleman / Strike-Convexity Domain of Raw SVI as a Finite Polynomial-Sign Formula
theorems.description: For the five-parameter raw SVI total variance with sigma >= 0, a fixed finite Boolean combination of signs of polynomials in (a, b, rho, m, sigma) holds exactly when b >= 0, rho^2 <= 1, the variance is positive at every log-strike, and the Black–Scholes call with the SVI volatility substituted strike by strike is convex in strike on (0, infinity). The kinked zero-scale slice sigma = 0 is included. This is an explicit quantifier-free construction of the domain MathFin issue #174 recorded as open: its atoms are signs of the coefficients of the degree-at-most-ten numerator polynomial and of the characteristic coefficients of four Hermite matrices (up to 9 by 9) over R[a, b, rho, m, sigma], per degree branch, plus two quadratic tests at sigma = 0. The formula is defined structurally and is not written out as a list of inequalities. No tail condition is included: the large-strike limit of the call (the strict wing slope b(1+rho) < 2) and an atom at zero are not addressed, so the set is the Durrleman / strike-convexity domain, which is how #174 states the problem, and not full butterfly-freeness; mf-svi-butterfly-free-sign-formula adds the tail condition.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.ExtendedFormula

open MathFin MathFin.SVI Set

/-- **The strike-convexity domain of raw SVI as a finite sign formula.**
    `extendedCertificateFormula`, a fixed finite Boolean combination of signs of polynomials in the
    five parameters, holds at `p` exactly when `σ ≥ 0`, `b ≥ 0`, `ρ² ≤ 1`, the total variance is
    positive at every log-strike, and the SVI-smiled Black–Scholes call is convex in strike on
    `(0, ∞)`. Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.extendedCertificateFormula_iff_bsSmile_convex`. -/
theorem svi_strike_convexity_sign_formula (p : Params) :
    extendedCertificateFormula.eval p = true ↔
      0 ≤ p.sigma ∧ 0 ≤ p.b ∧ 0 ≤ 1 - p.rho ^ 2 ∧
        (∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) ∧ ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) (bsSmile p) :=
  extendedCertificateFormula_iff_bsSmile_convex p

The raw SVI total variance is w(k) = a + b(rho(k-m) + sqrt((k-m)^2 + sigma^2)) and Durrleman's function g is built from its actual first and second derivatives (Derivatives.lean). The formula is a SignFormula over MvPolynomial (Fin 5) R, defined structurally as the expansion of a finite sign program (degree branch, four Hermite-matrix signatures by characteristic sign variations); it is not printed as an expanded list of inequalities. Proof route: rationalise g to a degree-ten polynomial on (0, infinity); nonnegativity there iff endpoint signs and no negative critical value; count those by four Tarski queries; evaluate each by Hermite's trace-form signature identity, proved for arbitrary nonzero f without squarefreeness; clear denominators. For sigma = 0 the slice is piecewise linear; each branch reduces to a quadratic nonnegative on a ray, and convexity across the kink follows from the upward jump of the one-sided derivative. SCOPE. The characterised set is positive variance together with convexity in strike of the normalised smiled call on (0, infinity). It is not full butterfly-freeness: no tail condition is proved (the call tending to 0 at large strikes, i.e. the strict wing slope b(1+rho) < 2, or the absence of an atom at zero), and monotonicity of the call is not stated. Slices with zero variance at some log-strike are excluded (for sigma = 0 that means a > 0). Whether the formula is minimal, or how large its expansion is, is not addressed. No statement about calendar-spread arbitrage.

theorems.name: Butterfly-Free Raw SVI as a Finite Polynomial-Sign Formula
theorems.description: For the five-parameter raw SVI total variance with b >= 0 and positive variance, d_+(k) tends to minus infinity as k tends to infinity exactly when the right wing slope b(1+rho) is below 2, and the SVI-smiled Black–Scholes call tends to 0 at large strikes exactly when b(1+rho) < 2. Adding the sign atom 2 - b(1+rho) > 0 to the strike-convexity formula gives a fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial signs that holds exactly when sigma >= 0, b >= 0, rho^2 <= 1, the variance is positive at every log-strike, and the smiled call C is a normalised call price function on positive strikes: convex, nonincreasing, max(1-K,0) <= C(K) <= 1, C(K) -> 1 as K -> 0+ and C(K) -> 0 as K -> infinity. Convexity, the two bounds and the large-strike limit are the single-maturity conditions of Roper's Theorem 2.1 with the forward normalised to one; butterfly-free here means these call-price conditions, and the last step of that theorem, constructing the nonnegative mean-one random variable whose call prices are C, is not formalised. The convexity part of the formula is defined structurally, not written out.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.TailCondition

open MathFin MathFin.SVI Set Filter Topology

/-- **The tail condition for raw SVI.** For `b ≥ 0` and total variance positive at every
    log-strike, `d₊(k) → −∞` as `k → ∞` exactly when the right wing slope `b(1 + ρ)` is below
    `2`. Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.tendsto_dpl_atBot_iff`. -/
theorem svi_tail_condition (p : Params) (hb : 0 ≤ p.b) (hw : ∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ ForwardSmile.dpl k (variance p k)) atTop atBot ↔ p.b * (1 + p.rho) < 2 :=
  tendsto_dpl_atBot_iff p hb hw

/-- **The call price at large strikes.** Under the same hypotheses the SVI-smiled call tends to
    `0` exactly when `b(1 + ρ) < 2`. Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.tendsto_bsSmile_zero_iff`. -/
theorem svi_call_tendsto_zero_iff (p : Params) (hb : 0 ≤ p.b)
    (hw : ∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) :
    Tendsto (bsSmile p) atTop (𝓝 0) ↔ p.b * (1 + p.rho) < 2 :=
  tendsto_bsSmile_zero_iff p hb hw

/-- **Convexity of the call and the tail condition.** `butterflyFreeFormula`, the
    strike-convexity formula with the one further sign atom `2 − b(1 + ρ) > 0`, holds at `p`
    exactly when `σ ≥ 0`, `b ≥ 0`, `ρ² ≤ 1`, the total variance is positive at every log-strike,
    the SVI-smiled Black–Scholes call is convex in strike on `(0, ∞)`, and `d₊(k) → −∞` as
    `k → ∞`; for `σ > 0` these are the two conditions of Gatheral–Jacquier's
    Lemma 2.2. Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.butterflyFreeFormula_iff`. -/
theorem svi_sign_formula_iff_convex_and_tail (p : Params) :
    butterflyFreeFormula.eval p = true ↔
      0 ≤ p.sigma ∧ 0 ≤ p.b ∧ 0 ≤ 1 - p.rho ^ 2 ∧ (∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) ∧
        ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) (bsSmile p) ∧ Tendsto (fun k ↦ ForwardSmile.dpl k (variance p k)) atTop atBot :=
  butterflyFreeFormula_iff p

/-- **Butterfly-free raw SVI as a finite sign formula.** The same formula holds at `p` exactly
    when `σ ≥ 0`, `b ≥ 0`, `ρ² ≤ 1`, the total variance is positive at every log-strike, and the
    SVI-smiled call is a normalised call price function: convex and nonincreasing in the strike,
    between `(1 − K)⁺` and `1`, tending to `1` at strike `0` and to `0` at large strikes.
    Re-export of `MathFin.SVI.butterflyFreeFormula_iff_isNormalizedCallPrice`. -/
theorem svi_butterfly_free_sign_formula (p : Params) :
    butterflyFreeFormula.eval p = true ↔
      0 ≤ p.sigma ∧ 0 ≤ p.b ∧ 0 ≤ 1 - p.rho ^ 2 ∧ (∀ k : ℝ, 0 < variance p k) ∧
        IsNormalizedCallPrice (bsSmile p) :=
  butterflyFreeFormula_iff_isNormalizedCallPrice p

metadata.reference: Roper, Arbitrage free implied volatility surfaces (2010), Theorem 2.1, for the call-price conditions; Gatheral and Jacquier, Arbitrage-free SVI volatility surfaces (2014), Lemma 2.2, for the tail condition; the strike-convexity certificate is Robert Martin's (MathFin issue #174, entry mf-svi-strike-convexity-sign-formula).
metadata.formalization_scope: Re-export of MathFin.SVI.tendsto_dpl_atBot_iff, tendsto_bsSmile_zero_iff, butterflyFreeFormula_iff and butterflyFreeFormula_iff_isNormalizedCallPrice (MathFin/Models/ModelFree/SVI/TailCondition.lean). IsNormalizedCallPrice C is the structure: C convex and antitone on (0, infinity), max(1-K,0) <= C(K) <= 1 for K > 0, C -> 1 at 0+, C -> 0 at +infinity. Proof. Right of m the variance lies between its asymptote a + b(1+rho)(k-m) and that plus b|sigma|, and d_+ = (w - 2k)/(2 sqrt w); for slope below 2 the numerator falls linearly while 2 M sqrt w <= q w + M^2/q, for slope at least 2 d_+ is eventually bounded below and sqrt w is eventually above any level. The call is a Black-Scholes price at the smile's volatility, so it is nonnegative and at least 1-K (bsV_nonneg, bsV_ge_forward_lower_bound at a standard normal), and at most Phi(d_+) <= 1; the limit at zero strike is a squeeze. A convex function on (0, infinity) bounded above is antitone. For slope at least 2, Phi(d_+) stays above a positive constant while e^k Phi(d_-) <= phi(d_+)/|d_-| tends to 0 by the Mills bound, so the call does not vanish. SCOPE. (1) The entry proves the single-maturity conditions of Roper's Theorem 2.1 on the call price function (convexity, the bounds, the large-strike limit) and two consequences (monotonicity, the limit at zero strike); it does not construct the nonnegative mean-one random variable (equivalently the risk-neutral law) whose call prices these are, which is the remaining step of that theorem. (2) Gatheral-Jacquier's Lemma 2.2 states butterfly-freeness as g >= 0 together with d_+ -> -infinity; here convexity of the smiled call stands in for g >= 0, and the two are proved equivalent only for sigma > 0 (bsSmile_convex_iff). At sigma = 0 the formula characterises convexity of the call, not the sign of g. (3) Slices with zero variance at some log-strike are excluded. (4) The convexity part is the structural, unexpanded formula of mf-svi-strike-convexity-sign-formula; the tail part adds one explicit atom. (5) Strikes are positive; the forward and discount factor are normalised to one. (6) Nothing about calendar-spread arbitrage or surfaces.

theorems.name: A Pricing Measure Gives a Normalised Call Price Function; a Market Pricing the SVI Smile Makes It Butterfly-Free
theorems.description: In a market with unit numeraire and a strictly positive asset S, priced up to T by a pricing measure Q, let F be the price of the claim paying S_T. Then k -> price(call at strike kF)/F is a normalised call price function: convex and nonincreasing on (0, infinity), between max(1-k,0) and 1, tending to 1 as k tends to 0+ and to 0 as k tends to infinity. This is the forward direction of Roper's Theorem 2.1 (a market gives a call price function), proved from the martingale property of the asset; the converse, a market with a nonnegative asset from a call price function, is mf-roper-converse. Composed with the SVI sign formula: if those normalised calls equal the SVI-smiled Black call bsSmile p at every k > 0, and sigma >= 0, b >= 0, rho^2 <= 1 with positive variance at every log-strike, then butterflyFreeFormula holds at p.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.MarketRealisation

open MathFin MathFin.Contracts MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **A pricing measure gives a normalised call price function.** With unit numéraire and a
    positive asset, the calls at the strikes `k F`, in units of the forward `F`, are a normalised
    call price function. Re-export of `MathFin.Market.IsPricingMeasure.isNormalizedCallPrice`. -/
theorem pricing_measure_call_price_normalized {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {M : Market Unit Ω}
    {T : ℝ≥0} {Q : Measure Ω} (hQ : M.IsPricingMeasure T Q) (hN : ∀ t ω, M.numeraire t ω = 1)
    (hpos : ∀ ω, 0 < M.asset () T ω) {F : ℝ} (hF : F = M.price Q (.pay T (.obs () T))) :
    IsNormalizedCallPrice fun k ↦ M.price Q (europeanCall (k * F) T) / F :=
  MathFin.Market.IsPricingMeasure.isNormalizedCallPrice hQ hN hpos hF

/-- **A market that prices the SVI smile makes the slice butterfly-free.** Re-export of
    `MathFin.SVI.butterflyFreeFormula_of_isPricingMeasure`. -/
theorem svi_market_butterfly_free {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {M : Market Unit Ω}
    {T : ℝ≥0} {Q : Measure Ω} {p : SVI.Params}
    (hp : 0 ≤ p.sigma ∧ 0 ≤ p.b ∧ 0 ≤ 1 - p.rho ^ 2 ∧ ∀ k, 0 < SVI.variance p k)
    (hQ : M.IsPricingMeasure T Q) (hN : ∀ t ω, M.numeraire t ω = 1)
    (hpos : ∀ ω, 0 < M.asset () T ω) {F : ℝ} (hF : F = M.price Q (.pay T (.obs () T)))
    (hsmile : ∀ k > 0, M.price Q (europeanCall (k * F) T) / F = SVI.bsSmile p k) :
    SVI.butterflyFreeFormula.eval p = true :=
  SVI.butterflyFreeFormula_of_isPricingMeasure hp hQ hN hpos hF hsmile

metadata.formalization_scope: Re-export of MathFin.Market.IsPricingMeasure.isNormalizedCallPrice (MathFin/Models/ModelFree/MarketCallPrice.lean) and MathFin.SVI.butterflyFreeFormula_of_isPricingMeasure (MathFin/Models/ModelFree/SVI/MarketRealisation.lean). Proof. The asset is a Q-martingale (unit numeraire), so S_T is Q-integrable with mean F > 0; X = S_T/F is positive with mean one, the call at strike kF in units of F is E[(X-k)^+]; convexity is that of the payoff carried through the integral (convexOn_integral_call), the intrinsic bound is E[(X-k)^+] >= E[X-k] = 1-k, the upper bound is (X-k)^+ <= X, the limit at infinity is dominated convergence, and monotonicity and the limit at 0+ follow (IsNormalizedCallPrice.of_convexOn). The SVI statement transports this to bsSmile p by the equality on (0, infinity) and applies butterflyFreeFormula_iff_isNormalizedCallPrice. SCOPE. (1) Forward direction only in this entry: the converse, a market with a nonnegative asset realising a call price function, is mf-roper-converse, and its SVI form is mf-svi-butterfly-free-market. (2) Single maturity, unit numeraire, a single asset, positive at T; the asset need not have a constant initial price. (3) The SVI statement assumes the market's normalised calls are the smile; it does not construct such a market. (4) Strikes are positive; no calendar-spread statement.

theorems.name: Roper's Converse: Every Normalised Call Price Function Is the Call Price Function of a Market
theorems.description: Let C be a normalised call price function: convex and nonincreasing on (0, infinity), between max(1-k,0) and 1, tending to 1 as k tends to 0+ and to 0 as k tends to infinity. Then there is a market with a single asset, unit numeraire and a pricing measure Q such that the asset is nonnegative at time one, the claim paying the asset at time one is worth 1, and the call at every strike k > 0 is worth C k. This is the converse direction of Roper's Theorem 2.1, for nonnegative asset values: the asset may vanish (a call price function can have an atom at 0, e.g. C(K) = max(1-(1-p)K, 0)), and a strictly positive asset is then impossible, so the statement is not claimed for positive assets. Single maturity, positive strikes, one asset; the market is the one-date market on the real line with the Breeden-Litzenberger law of C as both reference and pricing measure.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.RoperConverse

open MathFin MathFin.Contracts MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **Roper's converse.** Every normalised call price function is the call price function of a
    market with unit numéraire, a nonnegative asset at time one and a pricing measure under which
    the asset claim is worth one. Re-export of `MathFin.exists_market_of_isNormalizedCallPrice`. -/
theorem roper_converse {C : ℝ → ℝ} (hC : IsNormalizedCallPrice C) :
    ∃ (M : Market Unit ℝ) (Q : Measure ℝ), (∀ t ω, M.numeraire t ω = 1) ∧
      (∀ ω, 0 ≤ M.asset () 1 ω) ∧ M.IsPricingMeasure 1 Q ∧
      M.price Q (.pay 1 (.obs () 1)) = 1 ∧ ∀ k > 0, M.price Q (europeanCall k 1) = C k :=
  exists_market_of_isNormalizedCallPrice hC

metadata.reference: Roper, Arbitrage free implied volatility surfaces (2010), Theorem 2.1, converse direction.
metadata.formalization_scope: Re-export of MathFin.exists_market_of_isNormalizedCallPrice (MathFin/Models/ModelFree/RoperConverse.lean). Proof. The right derivative C'+ of the convex C is monotone (Mathlib), right-continuous (ConvexOn.continuousWithinAt_Ici_rightDeriv, proved here), between -1 and 0, and tends to 0 at infinity. The right limit of K -> 1 + C'+(K) on (0, infinity), extended by 0, is a Stieltjes function whose measure mu is a probability measure on [0, infinity) with mu(K, infinity) = -C'+(K). The layer-cake formula and the fundamental theorem of calculus for a right derivative give the integral of (x-K)^+ against mu equal to C K for K > 0, and monotone convergence as K decreases to 0 gives mean one. The market is Market.oneDate on the reals with reference and pricing measure mu, rate 0, date 1, and asset max(omega, 0); mu is a pricing measure (isPricingMeasure_oneDate), the asset claim is worth the mean, and the call is worth the integral of (x-K)^+. SCOPE. (1) The asset is nonnegative, not strictly positive: a normalised call price function may have an atom at 0, and a pricing measure equivalent to the reference measure gives a strictly positive asset no mass at 0, so the strictly positive version is false and is not claimed. (2) Single maturity, a single asset, unit numeraire, positive strikes; the forward is normalised to one. (3) The market is the trivial two-date one-date market, not a continuous-time model; no martingale or diffusion representation of the law (Kellerer, Dupire) is claimed.

theorems.name: A Butterfly-Free SVI Slice Is the Call Price Function of a Market
theorems.description: If the raw SVI parameters p satisfy the finite butterfly-free sign formula (butterflyFreeFormula), there is a market with a single asset, unit numeraire and a pricing measure Q such that the asset is nonnegative at time one, the claim paying the asset at time one is worth 1, and the call at every strike k > 0 is worth the SVI-smiled forward-normalised Black call bsSmile p k. The sign formula makes bsSmile p a normalised call price function and Roper's converse (mf-roper-converse) realises it. Single maturity (one), forward one, positive strikes; the asset is nonnegative, not strictly positive; no calendar-spread or surface statement.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.SVI.MarketRealisation

open MathFin MathFin.Contracts MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **A butterfly-free SVI slice is the call price function of a market.** Re-export of
    `MathFin.SVI.exists_market_of_butterflyFreeFormula`. -/
theorem svi_butterfly_free_market {p : SVI.Params}
    (h : SVI.butterflyFreeFormula.eval p = true) :
    ∃ (M : Market Unit ℝ) (Q : Measure ℝ), (∀ t ω, M.numeraire t ω = 1) ∧
      (∀ ω, 0 ≤ M.asset () 1 ω) ∧ M.IsPricingMeasure 1 Q ∧
      M.price Q (.pay 1 (.obs () 1)) = 1 ∧
      ∀ k > 0, M.price Q (europeanCall k 1) = SVI.bsSmile p k :=
  SVI.exists_market_of_butterflyFreeFormula h

Proof. butterflyFreeFormula_iff_isNormalizedCallPrice turns the sign formula into IsNormalizedCallPrice (bsSmile p), and exists_market_of_isNormalizedCallPrice (Roper's converse) gives the market: the one-date market on the reals with the Breeden-Litzenberger law of the smile as reference and pricing measure. SCOPE. (1) The asset is nonnegative, not strictly positive (a call price function may have an atom at 0). (2) One maturity, forward normalised to one, unit numeraire, positive strikes. (3) No calendar-spread condition and no SVI surface across maturities; no continuous-time model realising the smile.
